coin_collector_thief_coins_10.m: Sure. Let's see what you have.

coin_collector_thief_coins_20.m: [The coin collector eagerly examines the pilfered coins, eyes gleaming with fascination.]...

coin_collector_thief_coins_30.m: Ah, these coins tell a tale of clandestine dealings and shadowy alliances.

coin_collector_thief_coins_35.m: These bronze pieces bear the mark of the Lunar Whisper, an infamous thieves' guild that once ruled the underground markets. Legend has it, these coins were minted in secret, their alloy infused with fragments of moonstone to enhance the guild's stealthy endeavors

coin_collector_thief_coins_40.m: These silver coins hold the captivating history of a nomadic people, a seafaring tribe whose exploits were as boundless as the horizon. Born from the hands of skilled minters among the maritime wanderers, these coins tell the tale of the Ocean Nomads, a group of sailors, pirates, and free-spirited adventurers.

coin_collector_thief_coins_45.m: The silver pieces depict a mighty ship sailing under the moonlit sky, capturing the essence of the Ocean Nomads' freedom and unity. Legends speak of these coins being crafted during the tribe's grand gatherings, where sailors from various corners of the seas exchanged not only goods but also these tokens, forging connections that transcended the vastness of the ocean.

coin_collector_thief_coins_50.m:
[The collector pauses, his gaze lingering on the coins.] These pieces are not merely currency; they are artifacts of a hidden past,
a glimpse into the underground world where alliances were forged in secrecy. I'd be willing to make you an offer for these intriguing
tokens of history, should you be interested in parting with them.
r: So you want to buy them all?

coin_collector_thief_coins_55.m: Well, yes. But not all of them. Afterall, who needs 110 of these?
r: OK, so what do you want to buy?

coin_collector_thief_coins_60.m: Well, let's talk price first. You see, the silver coin is worth 11 gold in weight and the bronze is worth 5 gold in weight. But, to a collector they are worth more. Let's make this simple. I will pay you double those values for each coin and I'll take 5 of each.

coin_collector_thief_coins_65.m: 110 gold for the silver and 50 for the bronze coins.
r: Well, something is better than nothing.

coin_collector_troll_coins.m: Ah, these are Enchanted Coins, crafted by ancient wizards who once drew magic from the well's waters. The runes on these coins change patterns, a sign of their magical origin. Such artifacts are rare indeed.
r: What can you tell me about their enchantment?

coin_collector_troll_coins_2.m: The coins hold a faint echo of the well's enchantment. Though their magic is subtle, they carry the essence of the well's power. As a token of my gratitude for bringing these to me, I offer you this rare artifact in exchange for three of these coins. It is imbued with protective magic, much like these coins.
r: Without knowing more about this "rare artifact", I'm afraid that I will have to pass on your offer.
Umm, I guess I can trust you now.

coin_collector_troll_coins_3a.m: Well, if you change your mind, I will be here.

coin_collector_troll_coins_3b.m: For your effort in retrieving these valuable coins, take this rare artifact. It is a relic from the same era as the coins, crafted with similar enchantments. It will serve you well in your journeys, offering protection and a touch of ancient abilities.

r: I'm not a kid anymore. Let's talk about the Korhald coins.
Hey. I found the Korhald tomb and it had two items that I think might interest you.
Hey. I found the Korhald tomb and it had two items that I think might interest you.
Inside the  Korhald tomb, I found a locked chest. Do you know where I can find its key?
Hey. I need to go now and find this map.
I found these glowing coins in a pit beneath the well in Wexlow Village. They seem magical.
We have no more business to discuss. I'll see you later.
I found these glowing coins in a pit beneath the well in Wexlow Village. They seem magical.
I was glad to help fulfill you and your father's dream, but I need to go now.
[Lie]I have these bronze and silver coins that I "acquired" in a game of chance. I would like to know if you are interested in them.

gylew10.m: He once told me this story when I was very young about this magnificent coin collection called the 'Korhald coins'. So from a very young age I was fascinated.
r: You mentioned 'Korhald coins'. Who or what is 'Korhald'?

gylew10_1.m: You never heard of Korhald? He was the founder of Remgard. Anyways, back to my story...

gylew10_2.m: My father never mentioned the exact location to me, but from my efforts, I've ascertained a location near Remgard.
r: Great, I see where this is going. I need to go back to Remgard.

gylew10_2_1.m: It is far east of here near a place called Laeroth Manor.

gylew11.m: Yes, a place called Laeroth Manor.

gylew12.m: We have failed to retrieve it as the monsters are too strong. That's where you come in. What do you say? Will you help me?
r: Yes, of course, you need my help.
Pathetic creatures you two are. Needing the help of a child. I will do it.

gylew13.m: Then please head to the east and return to me when you find the Korhald coins.

gylew14.m: We will discuss this after you have completed the job. But remember, I am from Feygard and can reward you handsomly.
r: OK, but I have high expectations. Please be prepared to pay up.

gylew3.m: I am a rare coin collector. Have you ever noticed how some of your gold is more unique or older looking than others?
r: Honestly, I just use it to buy bonemeal.

gylew4.m: Great. Please let me see...agh, interesting.

gylew4a.m: You know that stuff is illegal and that you can get in serious trouble just for possessing it?
r: What can I say? I like to go rogue.

gylew5.m: This one here was cut during the rise of Elythara and is quite rare and valuable. But this other one here is a more common coin as it was cut during Geomyr's rule. While this one here is from a far off land and is a part of a larger collection that has long been broken up by past pirates and thieves.
r: [While pointing at a few of the coins in Gylew's hand, you ask:] What about those?

gylew6.m: Where did you get these coins?! [Gylew shows you a set of identical coins]
r: None of your business. Now get to the point.
It was a gift from a friend. Can we get right to what you want?
With all of my coins, do you actually think I can remember?
It was a reward for helping a mermaid.

gylew7.m: OK, I will get back to my ask of you now.
r: Um, is this going to take long? I have to find my brother.
Interesting, it really is, but I'm leaving.
Interesting. Please enlighten me some more.
OK. What do you have of value?
Now that's funny. A coin collector traded me his gold coins for my coins.
Now that's funny. A coin collector traded me his gold coins for my coins.

gylew7a_3.m: That was foolish of you. This is very valuable and you just gave it to me.
r: Well, what can I say? You caught me me wanting to be charitable.
Well, I just gave it to you because I was hoping for something special in return.

gylew8.m: Where did you get these coins?! [Gylew shows you a collection of identical coins]
r: I took them off of a dead guy.
I got them from a friend
I don't know. After all, I have looted many a gold coin in my travels.

gylew8a_1.m: What?! You went digging through his corpse?
r: Don't judge me. I was desperate at the time.

gylew8a_2.m: I must have them. All 10 of them!
r: OK. What do you have of value?
Nope. You can not have them.
Wow! I get 550 gold for the 10 I gave you?

gylew9.m: You see, I was raised in Feygard by my father who was commissioned to create gold coins. All he ever talked about was coins and we shared this common love.

gylew_attack_2.m: My trusty henchman will take care of you.
r: Oh, you need someone to help you?
Yes and I already gave them to you.
Yes, I found the Korhald coins, but you are not getting them...[Attack]
Yes, but I don't have them on me. I will go get them.

gylew_korhald_25.m: You did? Oh, yes, I remember now.

gylew_korhald_27.m: There are two locks! How can this be? Do you know anything about a second key?
r: Yes. In fact, I met a 'friend' of yours who told me all about it.

gylew_korhald_30.m:
[Gylew examines the chest]
What?! There are two locks! How can this be? Do you know anything about a second key?
r: Yes. In fact, I met a 'friend' of yours who told me all about it.
Your half-brother, Forenza. What a story he had to tell.

gylew_korhald_50.m: But I see that you did not listen to those 'stories' as you would not be here if you had. What did he tell you about the second key?
r: Well, for starters, he told me that he had it and he would not give it to me without a fight. Which of course, we did fight to the death for.
YES, and I loved doing so. Pathetic creature he was.
I was forced to. He gave me no choice.
[Lie] No, but I beat him up good and took his key.

gylew_korhald_70.m: I guess I should be saddened, but I am not. Can I have my brother's key now? I've waited a long time for these coins.

gylew_korhald_80.m: Thank you! It is so nice to finally be this close to my life's dream.

gylew_korhald_cop_0.m: Oh, really?! Let me see them and we can talk more.
r: [You show Gylew the Coin of Prestige and the Shield of the brave]

gylew_korhald_cop_10.m: Hmm...these are indeed interesting. Very interesting in fact.
r: [While trying to hold back the giant smile that you can feel growing upon your face, you ask 'why is that?']

gylew_korhald_cop_20.m: Well, for starters, this shield has the Korhald family crest engraved on its front side and clearly belonged to Korhald himself, but I have no use for such an item. Here take it.

gylew_korhald_cop_30.m: But this coin you have here is a completely different story. I don't know anything about it. Which makes me want it even more. Can I have it? I will reward you handsomely for it.
r: Reward?! I always love the sound of that. What are we talking here? {10000} gold? {20000} gold?
Here, take it. I have enough coins.

gylew_korhald_cop_30a.m: I don't know anything about it. Which makes me want it even more. Can I have it? I will reward you handsomely for it.
r: Reward?! I always love the sound of that. What are we talking here? {10000} gold? {20000} gold?
Here, take it. I have enough coins.

gylew_korhald_cop_35.m: Oh, you are so kind. I'll tell you what. Once you find your way to Feygard, seek out my family. They will help you make that shield a little bit better.

gylew_korhald_cop_40.m:
[While laughing]
Now, now, don't get greedy on me. How about {7000} gold and I will tell people we are friends?
r: Sounds like a great deal. I'll take it.
Let me think about it. I will be back shortly.

gylew_korhald_cop_45.m: OK, but don't keep an old man waiting too long. I want that coin.

gylew_korhald_cop_50.m: Excellent. Come see me if you ever find any more interesting coins.

gylew_old_man.m: Oh, you think you are a funny kid? I see.
r: Let's talk about the Korhald coins.
Yeah, actually, I do think so.
No way. I'm out of here.

gylew_old_man_10b.m: What are you waiting for? Go find those Korhald coins!

korhald_chest_examine_10_gylew.m: He opens the chest and begins to feverlessly sift through the coins, transferring each one to his bag. When to his surpirse, he finds something...

korhald_chest_examine_20_gylew.m: Look at what I found at the bottom of the chest. A pendant and a map. [Shows item to you]
r: A map? Really? Where does it point to?

korhald_chest_examine_30.m: Well, that is really hard to say. You see [he shows you the map], it is really old and a lot of the landmarks no longer exist in Dhayavar.
r: Yeah, I can see what you mean.

korhald_chest_examine_40.m: But not all hope is lost. You see this map shows the great river that is just right over there [points northeast] behind those trees. Anyone who follows the map going east, should have no problem reaching wherever this map is leading to.

korhald_chest_examine_50.m: Here, take the map and the pendant. If you need me, I'll be here for a little bit longer.

odd_coin_collector_ask_about_locked_ches.m: A locked chest you say? Well, I'm not really sure, but logic tells me to look back in the Laeroth Manor.
r: Oh, come on! I don't want to go back there again.

mermaid_scale.20: Crying and mourning, the mermaid called after him. Finally she cursed him. Since then, Tjure has never been happy. He just wanted to get rid of the scale. Nevertheless, he never ventured back to the vicinity of the river.
mermaid_scale.30: A wise woman told Tjure that he could neither throw away nor destroy the scale. His only salvation would be to give it back or to have someone buy it from him. But who would ever want to incur the wrath of a mermaid?
mermaid_scale.90: You decided not to help Tjure.
mermaid_scale.100: As soon as you held the scale in your hands, a great sluggishness and dispair came over you.

mermaid_scale.210: There rang out a beautiful song of gratitude.
mermaid_scale.220: You found a heavy bag of gold.
